title: 7 Best Driveway Cleaners in 2026: Match Cleaner to Stain
metaDescription: Zep Driveway and Concrete Concentrate is the best driveway cleaner for most slabs; add Oil Eater for oil, F9 BARC for rust and Wet and Forget for mildew.
keywords: what is the best driveway cleaner
intro:
The best concrete cleaner for most driveways is Zep Driveway and Concrete Pressure Wash Concentrate, because it handles the general mix of dirt, tire marks and light oil across a whole slab. Most driveways also carry one or two stains it cannot shift, so the real answer is a short kit: Oil Eater for oil, F9 BARC for orange rust and Wet and Forget for shaded mildew.

A blotchy driveway usually has three or four stain types at once, each with its own chemistry. Below are seven concrete cleaners for driveways ranked by what each one does best, followed by how to read your stains, which cleaners are safe on asphalt and pavers, and a start-to-finish washing method.
quickAnswer: For a dull, dirty concrete driveway, buy Zep Driveway and Concrete Concentrate and run it through a pressure washer. Add Oil Eater or Krud Kutter for oil spots, F9 BARC only where you see orange rust, and Wet and Forget for green or black growth in the shade. On asphalt, stick to water-based cleaners and keep pressure moderate.

Buy for the stains you can see. A degreaser will not touch rust, an oxygen cleaner barely moves old oil, and a rust remover does nothing to mildew. One general wash plus one specialist per stain type gets better results than any single all-purpose bottle.

These rankings are based on label claims and directions, product chemistry, surface compatibility and recurring owner feedback, not on hands-on trials.

sections.heading: The 7 Best Driveway Cleaners in 2026, Ranked
sections.body:
### Best Overall: Zep Driveway and Concrete Pressure Wash Concentrate

Zep's concentrate is built for washing a whole concrete driveway, which is the job most people actually have. It runs through a pressure washer's onboard tank or downstream injector, and it also works from a pump sprayer if you do not own a machine. The label targets the usual blend of dirt film, tire marks, organic grime and light oil drips. Mix it at the dilution the label gives for your setup, apply from the bottom of the slope upward so you do not leave clean streaks, keep it wet through the dwell time and rinse with a surface cleaner or a wide tip. Owners commonly report a noticeably brighter, more even slab after one pass. It is a finisher, not a specialist: heavy oil needs a degreaser first, and orange rust needs an acid-based remover. Gallon jugs are stocked at most home centers, and one jug typically covers a standard two-car driveway at label dilution.

**Pros:** Made for pressure washer detergent systems; handles mixed everyday grime; large jugs keep cost per square foot low; easy to find in stores.

**Cons:** Not strong enough for heavy oil on its own; does nothing for rust; best results need a pressure washer.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Zep+Driveway+and+Concrete+Pressure+Wash+Concentrate&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best for Gray Film and Organic Grime: Simple Green Oxy Solve Concrete and Driveway Cleaner

Oxy Solve pairs oxygen-based cleaning agents with surfactants, and that chemistry suits the dull gray film, leaf tannins and light algae that make a driveway look older than it is. Oxygen cleaners break down organic stains instead of just loosening them, which is why a shaded, leaf-stained slab can go from gray-green to pale in a single wash. It is formulated for pressure washer use and also works from a pump sprayer with a stiff broom. Because it does not rely on chlorine bleach, it is easier on lawn edges when you rinse well, though the label still asks you to wet nearby plants. Owners commonly describe an even brightening across the whole slab. Its limits are clear: it does little to old oil and nothing to rust or fertilizer stains. Use it as the general wash on a tired-looking driveway and pair it with a degreaser for the parking spots.

**Pros:** Lifts organic staining and dull film; works through a pressure washer or pump sprayer; gentler on plants than chlorine; brightens evenly.

**Cons:** Limited effect on old oil; best with a pressure washer; not a rust remover.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Simple+Green+Oxy+Solve+Concrete+and+Driveway+Cleaner&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Two-in-One: Krud Kutter Concrete and Driveway Cleaner Degreaser

Krud Kutter's driveway product sits between a pure degreaser and a general wash. It is water-based and meant to break down oil and grease while also lifting ordinary dirt, which makes it a practical single bottle for a driveway with a few drips near the garage and grime everywhere else. Scrub it into individual spots with a stiff brush, spray it over larger areas or run it through a pressure washer where the label allows. Owners commonly mention that it handles fresh and recent oil well and leaves a fairly uniform finish when used across the whole slab. Old, deep stains still need a poultice or enzyme product, because any cleaner like this only reaches what it touches during its dwell. On asphalt, read the current label for compatibility and test a hidden corner before treating the main area. The concentrate is the better value for whole-driveway work; ready-to-use sizes suit spot jobs.

**Pros:** Degreases and cleans in one product; brush, sprayer or pressure washer; water-based; suits driveways with scattered oil spots.

**Cons:** Weaker than a dedicated concentrate on heavy oil; ready-to-use sizes add up on big slabs; check asphalt guidance on the label.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Krud+Kutter+Concrete+and+Driveway+Cleaner+Degreaser&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best for Oil: Oil Eater Original Cleaner Degreaser Concentrate

Oil Eater Original is a concentrated, water-based alkaline degreaser that has been a fixture on shop floors for years. Its strength is petroleum: the label gives dilutions from light washing up to heavy-duty use, so the same jug can wash a slab or go after grease drips, tire marks and fresh oil spots. Pre-wet the concrete, apply, scrub with a stiff nylon brush, keep it wet for the label dwell and rinse with a hose or pressure washer. It also runs through many pressure washer detergent systems. On a driveway with heavy oil near the garage, it is the best first product here, usually followed by a general wash so the treated spot does not dry lighter than the rest. It is not designed for rust, fertilizer or algae, and like every degreaser it handles shallow oil better than stains that have soaked in for months. It is non-flammable but alkaline, so wear gloves and eye protection and keep it off aluminum trim.

**Pros:** Strong on fresh and recent oil and grease; flexible dilution; non-flammable, water-based; low cost per gallon of working mix.

**Cons:** Little effect on rust or organic stains; deep stains need a poultice or enzyme follow-up; alkaline, so protective gear is needed.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Oil+Eater+Original+Cleaner+Degreaser&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best for Rust: F9 BARC Rust and Fertilizer Stain Remover

F9 BARC comes from Front 9 Restoration, a brand used by professional exterior cleaners, and it targets the stains general cleaners cannot touch: orange rust from well-water sprinklers, iron-rich fertilizer granules, metal furniture and fasteners, plus some related mineral discoloration. Rust is iron oxide, a mineral, so degreasers and oxygen cleaners slide right over it. An acid-based remover dissolves it. The maker's directions call for wetting the surface, applying to the stain, brushing as needed and rinsing thoroughly. Owners commonly report that fertilizer speckles and sprinkler streaks fade fast, often in one application. Because it is acidic, wear gloves and eye protection, protect nearby plants and test first on colored, stamped or sealed concrete, where acid can change the finish. Never combine it with other cleaners, especially bleach. It costs more per bottle than a general wash, but spot work uses very little product.

**Pros:** Targets orange rust from sprinklers, fertilizer and metal; also used on some mineral stains; professional-grade; a little treats many spots.

**Cons:** Acid-based, so careful handling and rinsing are required; can affect some sealers and colored concrete; pricier than general cleaners.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=F9+BARC+Rust+Remover&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best for Mildew and Algae: Wet and Forget Outdoor Mold, Mildew and Algae Stain Remover

Wet and Forget works nothing like the rest of this list. It is not a scrub-and-rinse cleaner but a treatment: you spray it on a dry surface and leave it, and rain and time gradually wash away the dead mold, mildew, algae and lichen. The label says results typically take weeks to months, depending on weather and how heavy the growth is. That makes it a good fit for shaded driveway sections, north-facing paths and the strip under trees where green or black staining keeps coming back. It is bleach-free, and the maker gives instructions for protecting plants during application. It will not touch oil, tire marks or rust, so it complements a degreaser rather than replacing one. The key practical rule is weather: you need a dry surface and a dry window after spraying. If you need the driveway clean for an event next weekend, an oxygen wash is faster.

**Pros:** No rinsing or scrubbing; treats algae, mildew and lichen; bleach-free; covers large areas over time.

**Cons:** Slow, with results over weeks to months; no effect on oil or rust; needs dry weather after application.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Wet+and+Forget+Outdoor+Mold+Mildew+Algae+Stain+Remover&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Low-Toxicity Option: EF2000 Degreaser for Concrete

EF2000 is sold as a biodegradable cleaner and degreaser for concrete, engines and shop floors, and its appeal is easier handling. The maker markets it as non-toxic and non-caustic, which makes it more comfortable to use than high-pH degreasers when kids, pets or a vegetable garden sit right next to the driveway. It still lifts fresh oil, grease and general grime when you scrub it in and give it time. On heavy or old stains it is slower than an aggressive alkaline product, so expect extra rounds or pair it with a poultice. It goes on by brush or through a pump sprayer, and the label gives dilution guidance for different jobs. It is mostly sold online rather than on home center shelves. As with any cleaner, rinse thoroughly and keep runoff away from the storm drain, because even a biodegradable product carries the oil it lifted.

**Pros:** Marketed as non-toxic and biodegradable; effective on fresh oil and grime; gentler to handle than caustic degreasers; workable near landscaping with sensible rinsing.

**Cons:** Slower on heavy grease; harder to find in stores; old stains still need deeper treatment.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=EF2000+Concrete+Degreaser&tag=sktiger-20)

sections.heading: How Do You Choose a Driveway Cleaner?
sections.body:
Walk the driveway on a dry day and name the stains before you buy. Each color points to a different chemistry.

| Stain | What it looks like | What dissolves it | Pick |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Motor oil, grease | Black, slick, near the garage | Alkaline degreaser, poultice | Oil Eater, Krud Kutter |
| Mildew, algae | Gray-black or green, in shade | Oxidizers, biocides | Wet and Forget, Oxy Solve |
| Rust, fertilizer | Orange specks and streaks | Acid-based rust remover | F9 BARC |
| Leaf tannins | Brown leaf shapes under trees | Oxygen cleaner | Oxy Solve |
| General dirt | Even gray dullness | Detergent plus pressure | Zep concentrate |

### Why is oil the stain people underestimate?

A degreaser removes fresh drips, but a stain that has sat for months has moved into the concrete, and a cleaner only reaches the top. Those need a poultice or enzyme product; our ranking of the [best oil stain remover for concrete](/best-oil-stain-remover-for-concrete/) covers them.

### Take before photos

Concrete looks completely different wet and dry, and memory fades after an afternoon of scrubbing. Photograph the stains in the same light from the same spots, then compare dry photos the next day to see what actually changed.

sections.heading: How Does Driveway Cleaner Chemistry Work?
sections.body:
Four chemistries cover almost every product on the shelf.

### Alkaline degreasers

High pH plus surfactants emulsify oil so water can carry it away. They are the strongest option for petroleum stains and tire marks. Strong versions can dull aluminum, irritate skin and haze some acrylic sealers.

### Oxygen cleaners

These release active oxygen, typically from sodium percarbonate, which breaks down organic stains such as tannins, algae and mildew. They are gentler on plants than chlorine bleach and leave no chlorine smell.

### Acid cleaners

Acids dissolve minerals: rust, efflorescence and hard-water deposits. Formulated rust removers do this with less risk to the surface than straight muriatic acid, which etches cement paste aggressively.

### Biocides

Products such as Wet and Forget kill organic growth and let weather wash it off over time. Chlorine bleach also kills growth quickly but is harsher on plants and metal.

### Never mix

Bleach combined with acid or ammonia releases toxic gas. Use one chemistry at a time, rinse thoroughly between them and let the surface dry before switching to an acid product.

sections.heading: Which Driveway Cleaners Are Safe on Asphalt, Concrete and Pavers?
sections.body:
Concrete tolerates the widest range; asphalt and paver joints need more care.

### Concrete

Bare concrete handles high pH, oxidizers and diluted acids well. The risks are etching from strong acids and uneven lightening when you clean only some areas. Colored, stamped and sealed concrete are more sensitive, because some cleaners haze acrylic sealers and acids can shift color. Test on a hidden corner first. Once it is clean and dry, our [concrete driveway sealer reviews](/best-concrete-driveway-sealer-reviews/) cover how to protect it.

### Asphalt

What is the best cleaner for an asphalt driveway? A water-based product at moderate dilution. Blacktop is bound with a petroleum binder, so solvents and very strong degreasers soften it. Oxygen cleaners, biocides and many water-based degreasers are fine; read each label for asphalt guidance. Acids are rarely needed because rust shows little on a dark surface. For oil on blacktop, follow our guide on [how to remove oil stains from a driveway](/how-to-remove-oil-stains-from-driveway/), and for green growth see [how to remove moss from an asphalt driveway](/how-to-remove-moss-from-asphalt-driveway/).

### Pavers, brick and exposed aggregate

The units take concrete cleaners, but the sand joints are the weak point: high pressure blows them out and growth roots in them. Use moderate pressure, a surface cleaner and plan to refill joint sand after a deep clean. Keep acids to careful spot use on brick and aggregate, where they can attack mortar and loosen stone. If the pavers are sealed, see our [paver sealer](/best-paver-sealer/) guide for compatible products.

sections.heading: Do You Need a Pressure Washer to Clean a Driveway?
sections.body:
No, but it speeds up the rinse and gives a more even finish.

### Pump sprayer

A two-gallon garden sprayer lays down cleaner at the strength you mixed, which matters because pressure washer soap systems dilute heavily. Keep a sprayer just for cleaners and never reuse one that held herbicide.

### Pressure washer soap systems

Most consumer machines draw detergent only at low pressure through a black soap nozzle, often diluting the product to a small fraction of bottle strength. Choose cleaners labeled for pressure washer use and expect less punch than a sprayed application.

### Brushes still matter

A stiff nylon push broom works cleaner into texture and breaks up oil film far better than spraying alone. Brush spot stains; spray and let dwell for whole-surface washes.

### Rinse with a surface cleaner

A rotating surface cleaner gives a far more even result than a wand and avoids stripes. Our guide to the [best surface cleaner for a pressure washer](/best-surface-cleaner-for-pressure-washer/) explains how to match one to your machine. Without a machine, a high-flow hose nozzle and a stiff broom still work well with oxygen cleaners and degreasers.

sections.heading: How Do You Clean a Whole Driveway, Start to Finish?
sections.body:
Pre-treat spots, wash the whole slab, rinse evenly and judge it dry.

### Prepare

Choose a cool, overcast day or an early morning, because cleaner that dries on hot concrete stops working and can streak. Clear and sweep the driveway, wet nearby plants and block the storm drain or plan to send rinse water to lawn or gravel.

### Pre-treat

Put degreaser and a brush on oil spots and rust remover on orange stains, rinsing each thoroughly before the general wash.

### Wash

Apply the general cleaner over the whole slab, working from the bottom of the slope up so runoff does not streak dry concrete. Keep it wet for the label dwell, commonly 5 to 10 minutes, misting as needed.

### Rinse and judge

Rinse top down with a surface cleaner, overlapping passes by about a third, then finish edges with a wide-angle wand tip. A typical two-car concrete driveway takes about two to four hours. Let it dry for a full day before deciding what needs a second round; stains always look better wet.

sections.heading: How Do You Remove Rust, Fertilizer and Mildew Stains?
sections.body:
These are the three stains that make people think a cleaner failed.

### Rust

Rust is a mineral, so degreasers and oxygen cleaners do nothing to it. Use an acid-based remover such as F9 BARC as a spot treatment, then fix the source. Iron-rich well water from sprinklers is the usual cause, and adjusting the heads so they miss the driveway is the permanent fix.

### Fertilizer

Small orange or brown dots near lawn edges come from iron in fertilizer granules oxidizing on wet concrete. Blow stray granules off hard surfaces right after spreading, before rain or irrigation, and treat existing spots with the rust remover.

### Mildew and algae

An oxygen cleaner washes off current growth, while a biocide such as Wet and Forget kills what remains and slows regrowth. Trimming branches and improving drainage helps more than any chemical.

### Tire marks

Hot tires turning into a garage leave rubber and plasticizers. A degreaser and stiff brush lift them from bare concrete. On sealed concrete, some marks live in the sealer itself and only come out by stripping that area.

sections.heading: How Much Driveway Cleaner Do You Need, and When Should You Clean Before Sealing?
sections.body:
Compare cleaners by dilution and coverage, not bottle size, and clean at least a day or two before you seal.

### Coverage and dilution

A concentrate that dilutes 1 to 10 makes ten times the working solution of a ready-to-use spray. Pressure washer concentrates are often formulated so one gallon handles a standard driveway, while rust removers are measured in stains, not square feet. A general wash, a degreaser if you have oil and a rust remover only if you see orange will last most homeowners several cleanings.

### Cleaning before sealing

Every sealer maker requires a clean, dry surface, and cleaning is the single biggest factor in whether a sealer bonds. Oil, mildew and dirt film all interfere. On asphalt, oil spots also need an oil spot primer. Clean at least one or two days ahead, rinse thoroughly so no residue remains, and confirm water soaks in evenly before the first coat. For blacktop products, see our [asphalt driveway sealer reviews](/best-asphalt-driveway-sealer-reviews/).

### Plants, pets and runoff

Wet plants before and after, keep pets and children off until the slab is rinsed and dry, and keep wash water out of storm drains, which in most towns lead straight to creeks. Wear chemical-resistant gloves and safety glasses when mixing and spraying.

mistakes.title: Buying One Cleaner for Every Stain
mistakes.body: Degreasers do not dissolve rust, oxygen cleaners barely touch old oil and rust removers do nothing for mildew. Identify what is on the slab and buy one product per stain family instead of hoping a single bottle covers everything.

mistakes.title: Letting Cleaner Dry on Hot Concrete
mistakes.body: Most cleaners stop working once they dry, and dried residue can leave streaks harder to remove than the original grime. Work on a cool or overcast day, apply in sections and mist the surface to keep it wet through the label dwell.

mistakes.title: Spot Cleaning Without a Whole Wash
mistakes.body: Cleaning only the oil spots leaves bright patches surrounded by dull concrete, which can look worse than before. Pre-treat spots, then wash the entire driveway so the color evens out. On asphalt, sealing after spot cleaning does the same job.

mistakes.title: Using Muriatic Acid as an All-Purpose Cleaner
mistakes.body: Straight muriatic acid etches concrete, exposes sand, can discolor stamped finishes and gives off harsh fumes, and it does nothing for oil. Use a formulated rust remover only on rust and mineral stains, and degreasers or oxygen cleaners for everything else.

mistakes.title: Washing Residue Into the Storm Drain
mistakes.body: Driveway runoff carries oil, cleaner and debris straight to local waterways in most areas, and many towns restrict it. Berm or block the drain, send water to lawn or gravel where allowed, or collect it with a wet vacuum for proper disposal.

faqs.q: What is the best driveway cleaner?
faqs.a: For most concrete driveways, Zep Driveway and Concrete Pressure Wash Concentrate is the best single product, because it handles everyday dirt, tire marks and light oil across the whole slab. Add Oil Eater for heavy oil, F9 BARC for orange rust and Wet and Forget for shaded mildew. Matching the product to the stain matters more than the brand.

faqs.q: What is the best solution for cleaning a driveway?
faqs.a: A pressure washer concentrate applied from the bottom up, kept wet for its dwell time and rinsed with a surface cleaner is the most effective routine for a whole driveway. Pre-treat oil with a degreaser and rust with an acid remover first. On asphalt, use water-based cleaners only and keep the pressure moderate with a wide tip.

faqs.q: Will dish soap clean a driveway?
faqs.a: Partly. Dish soap is a mild degreaser that works on fresh oil spots, but it is weak for a whole driveway and can leave residue if not rinsed well. Laundry detergents with oxygen bleach can brighten organic stains. Purpose-made driveway cleaners are built for concrete, pressure washer dilution and outdoor rinsing, so they finish the job faster.

faqs.q: Is oxygen bleach better than chlorine bleach for driveways?
faqs.a: For most homeowners, yes. Oxygen cleaners break down tannins, algae and mildew, are gentler on plants and metal and do not give off chlorine fumes. Chlorine bleach kills growth faster but is harsher on landscaping and must never be mixed with ammonia or acids. Neither removes oil or rust, so pair them with the right specialist.

faqs.q: What is the best cleaner for an asphalt driveway?
faqs.a: A water-based cleaner labeled safe for asphalt, such as an oxygen cleaner, a biocide like Wet and Forget or a water-based degreaser at moderate dilution. Avoid solvent degreasers and very strong alkaline products, which can soften the binder. Test a small corner first and use a wide pressure washer tip held at least a foot away.

faqs.q: How often should you clean a driveway?
faqs.a: Once a year is enough for most driveways, plus a thorough clean before every sealing. Treat oil spots as soon as they happen, ideally within an hour, so they never set. Shaded driveways prone to mildew may benefit from a biocide treatment once or twice a year, usually in early spring and again in fall.

faqs.q: Do you need a pressure washer to clean a concrete driveway?
faqs.a: No, but it helps. A pump sprayer, a stiff push broom and a garden hose with a high-flow nozzle clean a driveway well, especially with oxygen cleaners and degreasers. A pressure washer with a surface cleaner rinses faster and leaves a more uniform finish, which matters most when you are cleaning ahead of a sealer.

bottomLine: The best driveway cleaner is the one that matches the stain in front of you. For most concrete driveways that means Zep's pressure wash concentrate for the whole slab, Oil Eater or Krud Kutter on the oil spots, F9 BARC only where you see rust and Wet and Forget for shaded areas that keep turning green, with EF2000 as a gentler degreaser around kids and pets. Pre-treat spots, wash the entire surface so it dries evenly, rinse with a surface cleaner, keep runoff out of the storm drain and give the slab a full day to dry before you judge it or seal it.
